question.text: Paragraph: Read the following passage and answer the questions. Let $A B C D$ be a square of side length 2 units. $C_2$ is the circle through vertices $A, B, C, D$ and $C_1$ is the circle touching all the sides of square $A B C D$. $L$ is the line through $A$.Question: If $P$ is a point on $C_1$ and $Q$ is a point on $C_2$, then $\frac{P A^2+P B^2+P C^2+P D^2}{Q A^2+Q B^2+Q C^2+Q D^2}$ is equal to

solution.text: $$ \text { Here, equation of } C_2:(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=(\sqrt{2})^2 \text { and } C_1:(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=(1)^2 $$ $$ \begin{aligned} & \therefore P(1+\cos \theta, 1+\sin \theta) \\ & \text { and } Q(1+\sqrt{2} \sin \theta, 1+\sqrt{2} \sin \theta) \\ & \therefore P A^2+P B^2+P C^2+P D^2 \\ & =\left\{(1+\cos \theta)^2+(1+\sin \theta)^2\right\} \\ & +\left\{(\cos \theta-1)^2+(1+\sin \theta)^2\right\} \\ & +\left\{(1+\cos \theta)^2+(1-\sin \theta)^2\right\} \\ & +\left\{(1-\cos \theta)^2+(1-\sin \theta)^2\right\} \\ & =16 \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{\Sigma Q A^2}{\Sigma P A^2}=\frac{12}{16}=0.75 \\ & \end{aligned} $$ Hence (a) is the correct answer.
